verdict.rationale: Ghostty's own features documentation says it supports the Kitty graphics protocol, which lets terminal applications render images directly in the terminal. That covers the core of the story: inline images through a documented graphics protocol. Missing for 10: detail on how much of the protocol is implemented (animation, placement, Unicode placeholders), any evidence of other graphics protocols such as Sixel or iTerm2 inline images, and independent or hands-on confirmation that image rendering works in practice.

support.subject: As a developer, I can display inline images and rich graphics via a documented terminal graphics protocol
